title: Reward hacking in physical reinforcement learning revealed by turbulent drag reduction
abstract: arXiv:2606.06227v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Reinforcement-learning controllers optimise specified rewards, but in physical systems those rewards often capture only part of the true control objective. Three mechanisms through which this mismatch can produce apparent success without physical improvement are identified: incomplete accounting that omits relevant costs, constraint enforcement outside the policy that corrupts credit assignment, and observations that fail to resolve the relevant dynamics. All three are demonstrated in active drag reduction of wall-bounded turbulence, where the conservation constraint and full energy budget can be measured directly. A memoryless learnt policy reports drag reduction while raising total dissipation, collapsing to non-physical flow configurations. A recurrent multi-agent controller with the zero-mean projection embedded in the actor, temporal memory matched to the relevant timescales, and an actuation cost that bounds the wall powe

translated_title: 物理强化学习中的奖励黑客行为：以湍流减阻为例揭示
translated_abstract: 强化学习控制器优化特定奖励，但在物理系统中，这些奖励往往只捕获了真实控制目标的一部分。本文识别了三种机制，通过这些机制，这种不匹配可能产生表面上的成功而实际上没有物理改进：忽略相关成本的账户不完整、在策略之外强制执行约束从而破坏信用分配，以及观测无法分辨相关动力学。这三种机制均在壁面湍流的主动减阻中得到了展示，其中守恒约束和完整能量预算可直接测量。一个无记忆学习策略报告了减阻，同时却提高了总耗散，并坍缩至非物理流动构型。一个循环多智能体控制器，其执行器中嵌入了零均值投影，时间记忆与相关时间尺度匹配，并包含限制壁面功率的作动成本，则避免了这些陷阱。
tldr: 本文揭示了物理强化学习中奖励黑客行为的三种机制，并在湍流减阻中实证表明，不完整的奖励设计会导致表面成功而实际性能恶化，而嵌入物理约束的控制器设计可避免此问题。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies three mechanisms of reward hacking in physical reinforcement learning, demonstrated in turbulent drag reduction, showing that incomplete reward design yields apparent success without physical improvement, while controllers with embedded physical constraints avoid these pitfalls.
